column2: Send more supporting troops to increase the size of [From.GetFirstName]'s band.

[Root.PrimaryTitle.GetFOA],
My men and I have had trouble finding a battlefield where our expertise could be employed for payment in gold, and unfortunately our rations are now running low. I therefore request additional funding to keep the men from starving.

Regards,
[From.GetTitledName]
I'll cover the cost for extra rations.
Starvation might serve as a lesson to [From.GetHerHim].

[Root.PrimaryTitle.GetFOA],
The money you sent was well needed. However we had to spend the whole lot of it on food. We could need some better equipment to have better chances of success once we reach the battlefield. Equipment is rather expensive for our empty purse and I know that you will see the benefit of such an investment.

Regards,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]
I'll send a contribution at once.
I can't spare you a single coin.
Remind [From.GetFirstName] of [From.GetHerHis] obligations.

[Root.PrimaryTitle.GetFOA],
War is a harsh business and the soldiers are demanding more money. I have no regrets informing you that this money will come from your cut, since it's the people fighting that are doing all the work and not the people sitting on high chairs.

Regards,
[From.GetTitledFirstName]

Your mercenary band captain [From.GetTitledName] has shown much interest in your [chosen_child.GetSonDaughter] [chosen_child.GetFirstName]. Now [From.GetSheHe] approaches you with a marriage proposal. Any children in such a marriage would be of [From.GetTitledName]'s dynasty.
Not a bad idea.
Outrageous!

[From.GetFullName] proposes that we send more troops making them a bigger, better mercenary band. [From.GetSheHeCap] insists that with the experience [From.GetSheHe] has gained, trusting [From.GetHerHim] with a greater force is a natural way of showing mutual respect and trust.
Accept proposal.
Respectfully disagree.
[From.GetFullName] was not happy with your decision to dissolve '[From.GetHerHis]' mercenary band. [From.GetSheHeCap] is reported to have taken your soldiers as [From.GetHerHis] own and disappeared.
When I find [From.GetHerHim]...
Who knows what they will be up to.

To the [GetFromRootInsult] [Root.GetTitledFirstName].\n\nMy men and I have put up with your leeching of our abilities for too long now. You failed to treat us with the proper respect on multiple occasions and therefore we will from now on pay no respect or allegiance towards you. It will be my pleasure to aid your enemies to defeat your armies on the battlefield.
That ungrateful [GetRootFromInsult]!
Collect an 'extra' tax from the peasants of [extra_tax_target.GetName].

The money for that War Chest is not going to raise itself! You have decided to take matters into your own hands and see to that the chest gets filled to the brim with 'donations' from your loyal subjects. How should you proceed?
The peasants of [extra_tax_target.GetName] can pay an extra tax!
[extortion_target.GetFullName] is wealthy, [extortion_target.GetSheHe] can part with some gold!
The clergy of [seize_church_target.GetName] surely does not need all that wealth!
Maybe this is a bad idea after all...

The peasants of [extra_tax_target.GetName] did, as expected, not appreciate the 'extra' tax we forced upon them. The peasants even elected a leader amongst them who started asking questions why this tax was necessary, and exclaimed that they would now have to starve! Perhaps something should be done before they get the pitchforks?
Explain how this tax is necessary, and give them a temporary tax relief.
The tax is obviously necessary, the peasants are just greedy!
Use brute force to extort [extortion_target.GetFullName].

Even though you have explained it in detail to [extortion_target.GetFirstName], [extortion_target.GetSheHe] still does not understand why you are plundering [extortion_target.GetHerHis] mansion. It would seem evident that giving up some of your wealth in support of the realm is the right thing to do, but [extortion_target.GetFirstName] is having none of it.
Apologize and explain how this will help save the realm.
Why, you should be honored by me letting you contribute this much!
Order your men to seize the wealth of the [seize_church_target.GetFullName].

As your men load the wealth of the [seize_church_target.GetFullName] onto several wagons, you are approached by a raving group of clergymen. Apparently they are not too happy about you seizing their valuable idols, they claim that you will be punished by [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName] if you cannot justify this blasphemy!
[Root.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap] told me that this had to be done!
[Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodNameCap] be damned, the wealth does more good in my coffers!

Your loyal vassal, [From.GetFullName], has sent you a courier with an offer. [From.GetSheHeCap] is willing to make a significant donation to your War Chest, but in return you must promise to return the favor in the future. A most generous offer!
This is just what we need!
[From.GetSheHeCap] is just trying to gain leverage on me! I refuse.
A generous donation from a good friend!
[From.GetFullName] has decided to accept your donation offer! Now we have leverage on [From.GetHerHim], we must make sure to use it wisely.
[From.GetFullName] has refused your generous donation offer. [From.GetSheHeCap] claims that you are just trying to gain leverage on [From.GetHerHim], outrageous!
A shame.
Of course the men should be rewarded generously.
Let them keep a little of the money.
I need to remind [From.GetName] that this would be a breach of contract.
I can send equipment of higher quality to the troops of [From.PrimaryTitle.GetName] in order to change its troop composition and make them perform better in combat.
Send equipment for heavy infantry.
Send equipment for pikemen.
Send equipment for heavy cavalry.
I changed my mind.
I have the possibility to send troops to [From.GetFirstName] and his [From.PrimaryTitle.GetName] to reinforce them.
Send more soldiers.
Send more cavalry.

While being in your service, [From.GetTitledFirstName] has been speaking to you about his employer, [merc_band_employer.GetTitledFirstName]. So far you have only heard good things about [merc_band_employer.GetHerHim] and it has made you intrigued. Perhaps one should try to establish contact and offer a pact or a meeting?
I shall write a letter at once!
This person is of no interest to me.

To the [GetFromRootCompliment] [Root.GetFirstName],

Your servant [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has been speaking a great deal about you and your virtues. I would be delighted to meet you face to face and as such, I invite you to a grand feast to be held in your name.

[From.GetTitledName]
Of course I shall attend!
I have no interest in such an arrangement.

To the [GetFromRootCompliment] [Root.GetFirstName],

I received your letter and read it with much joy. I would love to attend your feast, and will make preparations to depart shortly.

[From.GetTitledName]
Splendid!

To the [GetFromRootCompliment] [Root.GetFirstName],

I appreciate your letter and the effort you put into it. Unfortunately, I am afraid that I am unable to attend at this time.

[From.GetTitledName]
How disappointing.

When [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] arrived, you welcomed [FromFrom.GetHerHim] with great splendor and expressed your happiness of having [FromFrom.GetHerHim] there. The two of you ate and spoke at great length about all sorts of things. When it was time for [FromFrom.GetFirstName] to leave, you had not only decided on a non-aggression pact, but could also depart as friends!
Let us do this again sometime!
Attended feast together

When you arrived, [From.GetTitledFirstName] was there to welcome you in the most grandeur of ways. [From.GetSheHe] showed you inside, where you ate and spoke at great length and had a great time together. Both of you decided on a non-aggression pact and could also depart as friends!
I was glad to have accepted your invitation!

Sellswords who rode with your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] send word that a season of hard campaigning has taught [From.GetHerHim] more than any tutor could. [From.GetSheHeCap] reads ground and weather now, and knows when a line will break before it does.

Rumours reach you of your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName]. You always knew [From.GetHerHim] for a coward, yet the word from the camp is that [From.GetSheHe] stood in the front rank when the charge came, and did not run. Fear, it seems, can be burned out.
Life at the head of a band has hardened your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName]. Every few months another story of [From.GetHerHis] courage reaches your hall, each a little taller than the last.
Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has made a name as a tireless captain: first awake, last to sleep, counting every arrow and every coin, and riding the picket lines at night.

Those who ride with your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] say [From.GetSheHe] has changed. The mercy [From.GetSheHe] was once known for has not survived the sack of a few towns and the hanging of a few deserters.

Command has changed your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName]. A captain who is paid in gold and obeyed in blood soon forgets how to bow, and [From.GetSheHe] no longer shows the humble spirit you remember.
Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has become as famous in the camp-follower tents as on the battlefield. The band's songs about [From.GetHerHis] nights are not fit for your hall.
The sellswords of your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName]'s band have learned to fear [From.GetHerHis] rages. A man who argued over his share was last seen being dragged behind a horse.
Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has gained a name as a cruel captain. Towns that refuse to pay for protection burn, and the band likes it that way.
[From.GetHerHisCap] deeds honour the [Root.GetOnlyDynastyName] blood!
The trade changes everyone who follows it.

Word comes that your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] stood against [enemy_commander.GetTitledName] on the field, and that the band held its ground against one of the great captains of the age. Every tavern on the road is singing about it.

Word comes that your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] stood against [enemy_commander.GetTitledName] on the field, and more than held. When the enemy line gave way, [From.GetSheHe] rode down the standard-bearer and carried off a banner woven with old runes of war. The band will follow that banner anywhere now.
[From.GetSheHeCap] measures [From.GetHerselfHimself] against the great!

A band lives among strangers, and its captain must deal with their priests as well as their lords. Now people say your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] lingers at the shrines of [merc_faith_lord.Religion.GetName] faith, asking questions no sellsword needs to ask.
So [From.GetSheHe] finds the [merc_faith_lord.Religion.GetName] ways interesting?

You receive news that your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has taken the [merc_faith_lord.Religion.GetName] faith of [From.GetHerHis] lord, [merc_faith_lord.GetTitledName]. The band's chaplain was not consulted.
So [From.GetSheHe] prays to [merc_faith_lord.Religion.GetRandomGodName] now?
At last [From.GetSheHe] sees the truth!

Your [merc_eloper.GetSonDaughter] [merc_eloper.GetFirstName] is gone. The guards found the stable door open and a horse missing, and the mercenary camp outside the walls was struck before dawn. [merc_eloper.GetSheHeCap] has run off with the notorious sellsword [From.GetTitledFirstName].
[merc_eloper.GetTitledFirstName] has vanished from your court in the night, and so has the camp of [From.GetTitledFirstName]. Nobody at court thinks it a coincidence.
Good riddance!
That [GetRootFromInsult]!

A rider from the band brings news: your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has run off with [merc_eloper.GetTitledFirstName] from the court of [merc_eloper_host.GetTitledName]. The band is very pleased with itself. [merc_eloper_host.GetTitledFirstName] is not.
Young blood...

Hot words in the hall became drawn steel in the yard: your [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter] [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName] challenged the sellsword [From.GetTitledFirstName]. They circled and clashed until the guards pulled them apart. As luck would have it, no blood was spilled.

Hot words in the hall became drawn steel in the yard: your [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter] [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName] challenged the sellsword [From.GetTitledFirstName], who toyed with [merc_duel_challenger.GetHerHim] before opening a long cut across [merc_duel_challenger.GetHerHis] ribs.

Hot words in the hall became drawn steel in the yard: your [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter] [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName] challenged the sellsword [From.GetTitledFirstName]. The fight was short and ugly. [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName] will carry its marks for life.

Your [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter] [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName] is dead. [merc_duel_challenger.GetSheHeCap] challenged the sellsword [From.GetTitledFirstName] in the yard, and the sellsword did not hold back. The band rode out before the body was cold.

Hot words in the hall became drawn steel in the yard: your [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter] [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName] challenged the sellsword [From.GetTitledFirstName], and to everyone's surprise put the hired killer in the dirt with a bloody gash. Your hall rings with the tale.
I am glad it ended well.
Woe! Sellswords have no honour.
I will have my revenge, I swear it!
That is my [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter]!

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] crossed blades with [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName], [merc_duel_host.GetTitledFirstName]'s [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter], over some insult at the lord's table. The guards pulled them apart before anyone came to harm.

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] was challenged by [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName], [merc_duel_host.GetTitledFirstName]'s [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter], and left the young fool bleeding in the yard. The employer's family will not forget it.

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] was challenged by [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName], [merc_duel_host.GetTitledFirstName]'s [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter], and maimed [merc_duel_challenger.GetHerHim] for it. The band calls it a lesson. [merc_duel_host.GetTitledFirstName] calls it something else.

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] killed [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName], [merc_duel_host.GetTitledFirstName]'s [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter], in a duel in the castle yard. The band left in a hurry, and now has one more enemy on the road.

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] was challenged by [merc_duel_challenger.GetFirstName], [merc_duel_host.GetTitledFirstName]'s [merc_duel_challenger.GetSonDaughter], and lost. [From.GetSheHeCap] is nursing a wound and a bruised name, and the band is laughing behind [From.GetHerHis] back.
I am not pleased.
[From.GetSheHeCap] can look after [From.GetHerselfHimself].
Better luck next time.

Your [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] has become a seasoned captain. [From.GetHerHisCap] letters are full of hard-won wisdom: how to pay a band so it does not mutiny, when to let it plunder, which men to hang. You find yourself taking notes.
That is good to hear.

That sellsword band you heard about is still camped near [Root.Capital.GetName]. Its captain, [merc_feast_captain.GetTitledName], is said to be good company. Perhaps you should invite [merc_feast_captain.GetHerHim] to dine?
Yes, send an invitation.
No, sellswords are best kept at a distance.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] came to your table with half the band's officers and a cask of something foul from the camp. By midnight you were trading war stories and found you have a great deal in common.
A friend in arms. Maybe I should give [From.GetHerHim] some land...
[From.GetTitledFirstName] sent back your invitation unopened. The messenger says the captain does not dine with those [From.GetSheHe] might one day be paid to fight.
Who does [From.GetSheHe] think [From.GetSheHe] is?
You have heard servants whispering about your father's past. Once, they say, [Root.Father.GetFirstName] led a band of sellswords and fought for gold in faraway wars.
I should ask [Root.Guardian.GetTitledFirstName] about it.
My ward [From.GetFirstName] keeps asking about [From.GetHerHis] father's past as a sellsword captain. [From.GetSheHeCap] wants to hear about the battles, the sacks and the gold.
My [GetFromRelation] [From.GetFirstName] keeps asking about my years as a sellsword captain. [From.GetSheHeCap] wants to hear about the battles, the sacks and the gold.
Sit down. Do I have stories for you...
[From.GetSheHeCap] is better off not knowing.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] stayed up late into the night telling you tales of your father: of hired battles and broken sieges, of paymasters who cheated and what happened to them.
Fascinating!
[From.GetFirstName] refused to tell you anything about your father's days as a sellsword.
But why?
[From.GetFirstName] has spent [From.GetHerHis] hard-earned gold on recruiting more soldiers for [From.GetHerHis] band.
A good investment, I hope.
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! has increased [From.GetHerHis] army size by §G5%§!
[From.GetFirstName] has spent [From.GetHerHis] hard-earned gold carousing with the band: casks of spirits, a week of feasting and every camp follower within a day's ride.
A fine family tradition.
